clue.text: Flight path …

parts.note: a flight here is a set of stairs, so the route it gives is the way up through a building, not through the air

explanation.surface: An aircraft's route through the sky, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' wants to mean air travel; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is literally the path made by a flight of stairs, punning on the aviation sense.

clue.text: Says team never has a coherent plan

indicators.note: the phrase is read as having no letter A anywhere, so every A goes

explanation.surface: Someone claims a side lacks any joined-up strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never has a' strips both A's from SAYS TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised scheme or method of working.

clue.text: Old fellow supporting member in complete disaster

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting part sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
aged means old
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: An elderly man propping up a limb in a total catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final battle of the Bible, now any catastrophic conflict or ruin.

clue.text: Way to circumvent hindrance in risky venture

indicators.note: going round something, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a route is a way
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Finding a way round an obstacle in a dangerous enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as hindrance survives in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel game is a byword for any gamble whose outcome is pure chance.

clue.text: Separate technique dad's introduced …

indicators.note: brought in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: art is skill or technique
pa means dad; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A distinct method that father brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set apart are separate, held at a distance from each other.

clue.text: … stay to demonstrate it

definitions.meaning: staying power, the ability to last
the 'it' is the thing shown by holding out, the quality tested by trials of stamina

explanation.definitionFit: Stamina, or staying power, is the quality one shows by lasting out a long ordeal.

clue.text: Isolate distress signal

definitions.meaning: to abandon someone in an isolated place, as on a desert island
a firework rocket fired as a warning or call for help

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means strand alone; the noun is a flare fired to call for help at sea.

clue.text: Refer to crummy dive

indicators.note: shoddy, poorly made, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Telling someone about a shabby bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crummy' rearranges DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin 'see' is used in texts to point readers to another passage, directing them there.

clue.text: In the past, maybe Kelly has accepted one's suffering

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: taken in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw; maybe flags him as one example of a Ned
one is I, and 's stands for is, together I S

explanation.surface: Historically, an outlaw like Kelly took in one man's misery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a 19th-century Australian bushranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised describes someone in great pain or anguish, as an adjective of suffering.

clue.text: … making final approach?

parts.note: an aircraft on its final approach is closing in on the runway, so the phrase means getting close to something

explanation.surface: A plane coming in to land, continuing the flight of the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to 1 across, keeping the aircraft picture going; the question mark marks the loose, everyday reading of a pilot's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming ever closer to a destination is the plain sense of the phrase, a near synonym with an aviation colouring.

clue.text: American uncle and a youngster knocked back liqueur

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA

indicators.note: drinks are knocked back, and here the words a and youngster are turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout

explanation.surface: A family party where an uncle from the States and a youngster down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like the drinking, which suits the liqueur, but it turns the young animal and its article round; Uncle Sam stands for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an Italian anise-flavoured spirit, a classic after-dinner drink of that kind.

clue.text: Nothing done wrong in old theatre

parts.note: zero, the round letter O

indicators.note: done wrong suggests letters set out incorrectly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nothing was done badly at a historic playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old theatre' fits the ancient Greek building, not only the cinema chain later named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a roofed building for musical and dramatic performances bore this name, later borrowed by cinemas.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil — a chopper

definitions.meaning: a whisk used for whipping up eggs
slang for a helicopter, from its whirling rotor blades

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hand whisk and, in informal speech, a helicopter, whose rotors churn like one.

clue.text: They cover something new in ace pilot's qualification

parts.note: an ace in cards counts as one, giving A

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new is set inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pilot earns their wings, the badge of qualification

explanation.surface: Something novel in what an ace aviator must earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They cover something' looks like a loose lead-in, but it is the whole definition, cleverly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas sheets stretched over shopfronts or windows give shelter from sun and rain, covering what lies below.

clue.text: Note on monotonous song about LA? That's cool!

indicators.note: around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a chant is a repetitive tune

explanation.surface: A dull ditty about Los Angeles, praised as laid-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LA' looks like Los Angeles; it gives only its two letters, which sit inside the song.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is read as a description of someone casual and calmly unflustered.

clue.text: City where I'll take part in revolution

indicators.note: becoming part of something means sitting inside it, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a turn is one revolution, a full rotation
I will, read as the letter I being the subject

explanation.surface: A place where someone vows to join an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political upheaval; it is a single turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Succeed in delivering new issue?

parts.note: issue means offspring, so giving birth to new issue is to breed

explanation.surface: Managing to get a fresh magazine out on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a magazine edition; it is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed or have young is to make new offspring, the issue of the clue.

clue.text: Harassed communist removed evidence of membership

indicators.note: taken away, so one word's letters come out of the other

parts.note: badgered means pestered or harassed
Red is a familiar term for a communist

explanation.surface: A hounded party member stripped of proof that he belonged.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge worn on a lapel shows that the wearer belongs to a club or society.

clue.text: Soon to appear suitably elegant

definitions.meaning: about to arrive, read as two words
attractive and fitting, as in a dress that suits you

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word says about to arrive; whole, it means fitting and attractive.

clue.text: Council's sincerity only on the outside? Show agreement

indicators.note: only the outer edges of the word are kept, its first and last letters

parts.note: to nod is to signal assent

explanation.surface: A committee whose honesty is merely skin deep, asked to signal assent.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy, a governing council.

clue.text: Market to be entered by former tennis star, one that's washed up?

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them
Arthur Ashe, the American Wimbledon champion of 1975

explanation.surface: A trade show with a retired tennis great who is now a has-been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' suggests finished; it means cast ashore by the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The shells of sea creatures are carried in by waves and left on the beach.

clue.text: Listened to quiet man on board

indicators.note: what is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: peace means calm, quiet

explanation.surface: Someone paid attention to a calm sailor aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a ship's crew; it is a chessman on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen are called pieces, the figures moved about the board.

clue.text: Man with Arab connection, perhaps?

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, so this is a man joined to a horse

explanation.surface: Someone with ties to the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' suggests a person; it is the horse breed, the question mark flagging the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is the mythical creature with a man's upper body on a horse's body.

clue.text: Woman gathering information for items to be discussed

indicators.note: collecting in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A woman collects facts for the meeting's business.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of business for a meeting is its agenda.

clue.text: One burning out on a high?

definitions.text: One burning out on a high?

parts.words: One burning out on a high
parts.note: a shooting star burns up high in the sky

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted while euphoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning out' and 'high' suggest exhaustion and drugs; it is a shooting star.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a space rock burning up in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Hide significant details of case, but getting sorted out

indicators.note: the words are rearranged, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective's report that buries the key facts but still gets the matter resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges OF CASE BUT; 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make something deliberately unclear, obscuring the important points.

clue.text: Composer finally lost part of his income

indicators.note: finally points at the end of the composer's name, and lost says that closing letter is dropped

parts.note: César Franck, the Belgian-French composer

explanation.surface: A composer at last lost a share of his earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers to Franck, a Frenchman by adoption, paid in the old French currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was France's currency before the euro, so a coin of it formed part of a Frenchman's earnings.

clue.text: Distance restricting northern children's author

indicators.note: holding something within limits, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: a mile is a distance

explanation.surface: A gap that keeps a northern writer for young readers hemmed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh books for young readers.

clue.text: When first of colleagues retires, rise in branch

indicators.note: withdraws, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: to climb is to rise

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: When the senior colleague leaves, someone gets promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree's limb is one of its large branches.

clue.text: Mean to declare before a long time

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to announce something ahead of a lengthy wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend; it is the noun, the arithmetic average.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic average, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Funny comedian lacking energy for travelling

indicators.note: something funny is odd, so the letters are rearranged
going without, so a letter is missing from the pool

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired comic, short of energy, on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges COMEDIAN, and 'lacking' drops its E, leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples move from place to place rather than settling, roaming as a way of life.

clue.text: Flight to be taken at a standstill?

definitions.text: Flight to be taken at a standstill?

parts.words: Flight to be taken at a standstill
parts.note: a flight of moving stairs carries you up while you stand still on it

explanation.surface: A plane trip somehow made without moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' again suggests air travel; it is a flight of steps that does the moving for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving stairs carry riders between floors while they stand, the flight doing the climbing.
